findings.passage: I believe you should be required to present a photo ID in order to be able to vote.
findings.note: Floor remarks ahead of the vote to begin debate on the SAVE America Act (release from his Senate site). He backs a photo ID requirement and citizen-only voting.

findings.passage: “American voters in 36 states already show an ID to vote in elections. In my home state of Wyoming, we have voter ID laws. And getting your voter ID is free.
findings.note: Says Wyoming has voter ID and that the ID is free; says the SAVE America Act builds on current law.

findings.passage: “Voter ID and proof of citizenship are safeguards for our elections, not restrictions.
findings.note: Argues photo ID and proof of citizenship are safeguards, and rejects the claim that they suppress turnout.

findings.passage: I believe you should have to present a photo identification card in order to vote.
findings.note: Remarks at a press conference on the SAVE America Act.

findings.passage: The SAVE America Act requires two things.
findings.note: Floor remarks as prepared. In the next two sentences he lists the two requirements: a photo ID to vote and proof of citizenship to register.

findings.passage: One – Show a photo ID in order to vote. Two – Show proof of citizenship to register to vote.
findings.note: His own summary of what the SAVE America Act requires.

findings.passage: In many of these same states, obtaining a driver’s license automatically registers someone to vote.
findings.note: Raises driver's-license automatic registration and non-citizens on voter rolls as a related concern (Oregon example).
subjects: automatic voter registration through driver's license

findings.passage: The SAVE America Act simply says you need to be a citizen of America to register to vote.
findings.note: Floor remarks as prepared on photo ID and citizenship to register.

findings.passage: Thirty-six states in America, including Wyoming, require voters to present an ID when arriving at the polls.
findings.note: Points to state practice, including Wyoming, as support for photo ID.

findings.passage: It simply requires a photo ID when Americans show up to vote.
findings.note: Remarks on the Husted amendment to the SAVE America Act, a photo-ID-only amendment.

findings.passage: Voters can use a driver’s license.
findings.note: Describes the accepted ID types in the amendment; the next sentences name state ID, U.S. passport, military ID and tribal ID.

findings.passage: It does not touch voter rolls.
findings.note: Says the Husted photo-ID amendment does not change voter rolls (next sentence: it does not touch mail-in voting).

findings.passage: Illegal immigrants are not permitted to vote in federal elections.
findings.note: Floor remarks as prepared, on barring immigration enforcement at polling places; says non-citizens may not vote in federal elections.

findings.passage: When it comes to elections in America, only American citizens should be allowed to vote.
findings.note: Floor remarks as delivered, after New Jersey reported non-citizens on its voter rolls.

findings.passage: States need to clean up their voter rolls aggressively and do it immediately.
findings.note: Calls on states to clean voter rolls and cites the National Voter Registration Act.

findings.passage: At a time like this, Americans want to make sure that our own elections are safe and secure and fair.
findings.note: Floor remarks on House Bill Number One (H.R. 1, 2021 elections bill); general election integrity remarks, no ID detail in the excerpt read.

findings.motion: Cloture on Husted Amdt. 4732 to S. 1383: to require voters to provide photo identification. Result 53-47, rejected.

findings.note: Voted yes on ending debate on a photo ID bill.
